clue.text: Wet person missing an identity

indicators.note: missing tells us the word an is lacking from the person, so those letters drop out

parts.note: a person is a human
ID is the short form of identity, as on an ID card

explanation.surface: A soggy figure has lost track of who they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' could mean feeble, a British sense, but here it means damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Humid air is damp and muggy, so wet in the sense of moisture-laden weather.

clue.text: Measure pi

parts.note: read as an instruction, half of the word pint is the letters P and I, which is what the clue shows

explanation.surface: An instruction to calculate the circle constant.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: 'pi' is the result of taking half of 'pint', so the instruction 'half pint' produces it.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-pint is a unit of volume for beer or milk, so it is a measure.

clue.text: Instant introduction to good university with backing from oil baron

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter
the backing, or rear, of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An oil tycoon instantly funds a good university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil baron' looks like the definition, but oil supplies its final letter and baron alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful tycoon, so a business magnate, which is what baron means here.

clue.text: Policeman found in cheap bar outside either city, oddly

indicators.note: outside means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a dive is a seedy, cheap bar

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the words

explanation.surface: An officer turns up in a rough pub in one of two towns, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' could signal an anagram, but here it takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters of 'either city'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain-clothes investigator in the force is a policeman, one specialised in solving crimes.

clue.text: Dad leaves hitchhiker, say, on Middle East express

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece sitting on another follows it, so the shortened word comes after Middle East
leaves means departs from, so Dad is removed from the hitchhiker word

parts.note: a hitchhiker is an example of a passenger, hence say
Pa is an informal word for a father

explanation.surface: A father abandons a roadside thumber and takes a fast route east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' looks like an adjective or a verb, but here it is a noun: a courier sent specially.
explanation.definitionFit: An express is an urgent courier sent specially, the same role as a dispatch rider or envoy.

clue.text: Half-hearted runner's head dropping — Farah starts keener

indicators.note: starts means comes first, so the athlete's name opens the word

parts.note: Mo Farah is the British Olympic distance runner

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter; dropping moves it lower down
the heart of the word is its double N; half-hearted keeps only one of them

parts.note: taken as written, the word runner

explanation.surface: A tired runner falls behind as Mo Farah sets off eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' trims RUNNER to RUNER; 'head dropping' moves R down to give URNER. 'keener' looks like an adjective, but it is one who wails.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief, so a keener is one who laments the dead.

clue.text: Involved in impure boss's return to regain control

indicators.note: return means come back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
involved in says the letters are contained within the words

explanation.surface: A corrupt boss's comeback is about taking charge again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved in' finds PUREBOS in 'imPURE BOSs'; 'return' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting over drunkenness means recovering your self-command, so regaining control of oneself.

clue.text: Attitude from French and American prostitutes

parts.note: et is French for and
hos is US slang for prostitutes

explanation.surface: A disapproving view coming from sex workers on both sides of the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French and' is the French word for 'and', ET.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or outlook of a group, so a shared attitude.

clue.text: Travel from German holiday home, going North with six-footer

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a villa is a holiday home
an ant is an insect, and insects have six feet

explanation.surface: Setting off from a German villa, heading north with a very tall companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going North' reverses VILLA to ALLIV in a down clue. 'six-footer' suggests a tall person, but means an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To gad about from place to place in search of fun is to roam or travel.

clue.text: Rule restricting soldier's first leave

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the rule goes round the soldier's letter

parts.note: to reign is to rule

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A regulation stops a soldier taking leave for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' suggests army leave, but it is the verb: to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down from a post is to quit or leave it.

clue.text: Shiner's mild swelling

parts.note: light means mild, as in a light breeze or light punishment
a bulb is a rounded swelling, as at the base of a stem

explanation.surface: Someone's black eye is only a small lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shiner' suggests a black eye, which fits 'swelling'; here it is anything that shines. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp's glass globe glows, so it is literally something that shines.

clue.text: The man left Girl Guides

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
Ms is a title used for a woman

explanation.surface: A man walked out on the Girl Guides organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl Guides' reads as the youth movement, but the words split: Girl gives MS and Guides is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer a vessel or organisation is to be at its tiller, so the verb means directs or steers.

clue.text: It has flashing lights, potentially splicing corneas

indicators.note: potentially says the letters could become something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Something flashing could, in principle, damage the surface of the eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with push-button lights and flashing amber for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: These road crossings use signals whose amber phase blinks, so the definition describes a feature of one.

clue.text: More turbulent, revolutionary architecture is Ionic internally

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the hidden letters are read backwards
internally says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A daring building style keeps Greek columns on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internally' takes REISION from 'architectuRE IS IONic'; 'revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent seas or crowds are loud and rough, so more turbulent is a comparative of rowdy.

clue.text: Indiscreet book comes out after Trump/Biden chaos

indicators.note: comes out says the book letter is taken away from the pool of letters
chaos signals disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rash memoir appears after the turmoil of the Trump versus Biden election.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove B from TRUMPBIDEN; 'chaos' rearranges the remaining TRUMPIDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means unwise or rash, and indiscreet means careless in what one says or does.

clue.text: Fast bowler drops energy for game

indicators.note: drops means lets go of, so the energy letter falls out of the bowler

parts.note: a paceman is a fast bowler in cricket
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A quick cricket bowler runs out of steam during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a fast bowler is a paceman; 'drops' removes its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Pac-Man is a classic 1980s arcade video game of a yellow disc eating dots in a maze.

clue.text: Bend rule over V&A replacing lecturer in the arts

indicators.note: replacing means one thing takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: culture means the arts collectively

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so rule comes before the museum

parts.note: the V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

explanation.surface: A London museum's rule bends when it replaces an arts lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps L in CULTURE for R and VA. The V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum of art and design.
explanation.definitionFit: Curvature is the degree to which something curves, so a bend or arc.

clue.text: Went hunting earlier

definitions.meaning: hunted for prey, as a predator does

explanation.surface: Someone went hunting before everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: One reading is pre-dated, came before in time; the other is predated, hunted as a predator does.
explanation.definitionFit: A predator preys on others, and to pre-date something is to precede it in time.

clue.text: Go during school lecture

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: go is a euphemism for urinating, as is pee

explanation.surface: Someone nips out to the loo while a school talk is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is the euphemism for relieving oneself, not to leave or to try.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecture is a formal address to an audience, the same thing as a talk.

clue.text: Share kiss, both naked, with sex appeal — it's hot stuff

indicators.note: naked means stripped of outer covering, so each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A steamy encounter: undressed lovers share a kiss, and the attraction is hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both naked' strips the outer letters from both Share and kiss, giving HAR and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a fiery North African chilli paste, so it is spicy, hot food.

clue.text: Copper and informant — or superintendent

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a rat is slang for an informer

explanation.surface: A police officer and a grass, or perhaps their senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'superintendent' suggest police ranks; copper is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum keeper oversees and manages a collection, so superintendent in its sense of someone in charge.

clue.text: Opiate supplied by Morse, perhaps by means of pill

parts.note: Morse is an example of a code
in can mean by way of, as in paying in cash
E is slang for an ecstasy pill

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse provides painkillers in tablet form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morse' suggests the fictional detective, but it is the signalling code.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is a drug derived from opium, used as a painkiller, so a member of the opiate class.

clue.text: Shorten second wave

parts.note: to crimp hair is to put waves in it

explanation.surface: Cutting hair short and then giving it a quick wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shorten' and 'wave' suggest a haircut, but the definition means to skimp.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to stint or cut back, making something smaller or shorter than it should be.

clue.text: Obviously guilty — after a drop of cider, anything embarrassed script editor

indicators.note: a drop of a drink is a tiny amount, so just the first letter is taken

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything
embarrassed people go red
hand means handwriting, a script

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy on cider blushes over an editor's script that gives them away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'script' is handwriting, which is a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being found with blood still on one's hands means guilt is plain to see, an idiom for being found in the act.

clue.text: Greeting seen when Rachel and Louise meet

indicators.note: only the tail of the first name is seen at the point where the two names touch, so its front goes

parts.note: the name Rachel taken as written

indicators.note: where the names meet, only the front of the second name is kept, so its tail goes

parts.note: the name Louise taken as written

explanation.surface: Two women say hi when they run into each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter means a word hidden where the names join, racHEL LOuise, with 'and' skipped. Strictly that skip is loose, so 'seen' and 'meet' are shown as trimming each name to the letters at the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the everyday salutation said on meeting someone, so a word of welcome.

clue.text: Shot afternoon play

parts.note: a dram is a small shot of whisky
A is a rare abbreviation for afternoon, used by this setter before

explanation.surface: A quick drink before an afternoon show.
explanation.walkthrough: A for afternoon is unusual and not in most dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a work for the stage, so a theatrical play.

clue.text: Perfect if diet all evens out

indicators.note: evens out says the even-numbered letters are dropped, leaving the odd ones

explanation.surface: A diet works out flawlessly when everything balances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evens out' sounds like balancing, but it removes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal and perfect are synonyms: both describe something that could not be better.

clue.text: It's exciting, kinky Latin smut

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Kinky Latin filth is thrilling, the clue claims.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulant is anything that rouses or arouses, such as caffeine, so it is something that excites.

clue.text: Record over last bit of Don't Look Back In Anger — it can reduce the buzzing sound

definitions.text: it can reduce the buzzing sound

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the record's letters are read backwards

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter
In places the reversed look inside the anger word

parts.note: rage is a synonym of anger

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the letters of look are turned round

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Taping over an Oasis song, the setter suggests, quietens the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't Look Back In Anger' is an Oasis song, split into pieces. The answer is obscure: treating water with petrol to kill mosquito larvae.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading petrol on standing water kills mosquito larvae, so the treatment cuts down the insects that whine.

clue.text: It's beastly language that Björk uses, renouncing two independent clubs

indicators.note: renouncing means giving up, so the letters for two independents and two clubs are discarded

parts.note: Björk is an Icelandic singer, so she speaks Icelandic

indicators.note: two says the pair of letters that follows is taken twice over

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: A nasty tongue spoken by a singer who has quit two clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renouncing' removes IC from both ends of ICELANDIC. 'beastly' looks like 'nasty' but means 'a beast'.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is an African antelope, so it is a beast, an animal.
